claims.text: Candidates like this will keep using anti‑LGBT tactics for quite a bit longer.
The rise of social media is the key to this persistence.

implicit_assumptions: C1 is based on the assumption that the US timeline predicts other countries’ timelines
C2 assumes that social media exposure directly influences political messaging
Both assume similarity in sociopolitical contexts between the US and other countries
scope_notes: Generalization applies to unspecified future candidates in unspecified countries
Time frame inferred only from US example

Inference.supporting_quote: If it took us this long, it'll take countries like those much longer
Inference.premise: US legalization of gay marriage took 10 years
Inference.conclusion: Other countries will also have to wait a similarly long period
Inference.defective_inference: drawing a broad generalization about all other countries from the single US example
Inference.strongest_nonfallacious_reading: It is simply an observation that US took 10 years, no speculation that other countries will conform to that timeline.
Inference.auxiliary_observation: The comment does not present an explicit appeal to authority, majority, tradition, or other listed fallacies.

Evidence.supporting_quote: If it took us this long, it'll take countries like those much longer
Evidence.premise: US timeline is used to generalize about other countries
Evidence.conclusion: Other countries will take much longer to stop anti‑LGBT tactics
Evidence.strongest_nonfallacious_reading: No clear causal link established, merely a speculative comparison.
